Hi Asha — thanks for flagging this.

Short answer: we think Calendly is presenting local times using the visitor locale + daylight-saving offset in a way that maps some slots to quarter-hour boundaries for Australasian timezones. It's a known Calendly UI quirk when locale detection conflicts with the event's base timezone.

Workarounds I can do right now:
- I can send a manual .ics for the slot you want (I recommend 2029-07-03 11:00 NZST).
- You can change the timezone picker in the Calendly header (click the timezone label and set to "(GMT+12:00) Auckland" explicitly) — that usually normalizes the shown times.
- If you'd prefer, I can paste two fixed UTC options and you can confirm which one maps to 11:00 your side.

I'm looping in Chloe to send an ICS and the short agenda. Chloe — can you create an invite for 2029-07-03 11:00 NZST (UTC+12) and attach it here? Also note: NZ will enter a DST change in September, so this July slot is stable.

Sofia

Quick note on troubleshooting so we keep replies consistent:
1) Tell customers to explicitly set the timezone control in the Calendly page rather than relying on auto-detect. The control is small and easy to miss.
2) If they see minute offsets, send a manual ICS (we generate invites in UTC and label the local zone) — that's our reliable fallback.
3) If they insist on using Chili Piper/instant-booking, escalate to SRE to confirm the booking webhook preserves tz info (we had one webhook misinterpreting offsets last quarter).
